In [[geometry]], the '''augmented sphenocorona''' is the [[Johnson solid]] that can be constructed by attaching an [[equilateral square pyramid]] to one of the square faces of the [[sphenocorona]]. It is the only Johnson solid arising from "cut and paste" manipulations where the components are not all prisms, antiprisms or sections of [[Platonic solid|Platonic]] or [[Archimedean solid|Archimedean]] solids.

== Construction ==
The augmented sphenocorona is constructed by attaching [[equilateral square pyramid]] to the [[sphenocorona]], a process known as the [[Augmentation (geometry)|augmentation]]. This pyramid covers one square face of the sphenocorona, replacing it with four equilateral triangles. As a result, the augmented sphenocorona has 16 equilateral triangles and 1 square as its faces.{{r|berman}} The convex polyhedron with [[Regular polygon|regular]] faces is the [[Johnson solid]]; the augmented sphenocorona is one of them, enumerated as <math> J_{87} </math>, the 87th Johnson solid.{{r|francis}}

== Properties ==
For the edge length <math> a </math>, the surface area of an augmented sphenocorona is by summing the area of 16 equilateral triangles and 1 square:{{r|berman}}
<math display="block"> \left(1+4\sqrt{3}\right)a^2\approx7.92820a^2,</math>
Its [[volume]] can be calculated by slicing it into a sphenocorona and an equilateral square pyramid, and adding the volume subsequently:{{r|berman}}
<math display="block"> \left(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{1 + 3 \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} + \sqrt{13 + 3 \sqrt{6}}}+\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}\right)a^3\approx1.75105a^3.</math>
